name: Andromeda Galaxy
description: The closest large spiral galaxy to the Milky Way, visible to the naked eye under dark skies.

name: Whirlpool Galaxy
description: A classic spiral galaxy, notable for its clearly defined spiral structure and companion galaxy.

name: Pinwheel Galaxy
description: A grand design spiral galaxy, one of the largest and most detailed on the Messier list.

name: Triangulum Galaxy
description: The third-largest member of the Local Group of galaxies, fainter but large in angular size.

name: Bode's Galaxy
description: A grand spiral galaxy, famous for its perfect spiral arms and active star formation.

name: Cigar Galaxy
description: A starburst galaxy with a massive rate of star formation, interacting with M81.

name: Sombrero Galaxy
description: A spiral galaxy notable for its prominent dust lane and high surface brightness.

name: Black Eye Galaxy
description: Known for its spectacular dark band of dust obscuring the bright nucleus.

name: Centaurus A
description: A prominent elliptical galaxy and one of the closest radio galaxies to Earth.

name: Sculptor Galaxy
description: A large and bright starburst spiral galaxy in the Sculptor Group.

name: Orion Nebula
description: A vast region of star formation, easily the brightest diffuse nebula in the sky.

name: Ring Nebula
description: A prominent planetary nebula, the remnant of a star that shed its outer layers.

name: Lagoon Nebula
description: A giant interstellar cloud and H II region where active star formation is occurring.

name: Crab Nebula
description: A supernova remnant from a star explosion witnessed in 1054 AD.

name: Dumbbell Nebula
description: The first planetary nebula ever discovered, resembling an hourglass or dumbbell shape.

name: Helix Nebula
description: One of the closest planetary nebulae, earning it the nickname 'The Eye of God'.

name: North America Nebula
description: A large emission nebula whose shape resembles the continent of North America.

name: Veil Nebula
description: A large, faint supernova remnant in the constellation Cygnus.

name: Cat's Eye Nebula
description: One of the most complex planetary nebulae, known for its intricate structure.

name: Trifid Nebula
description: A combination of an open cluster, an emission nebula, a reflection nebula, and a dark nebula.

name: Rosette Nebula
description: A large, roughly circular star-forming region whose appearance resembles a rose.

name: Pleiades Cluster
description: One of the most famous open star clusters, known as the 'Seven Sisters'.

name: Hercules Globular Cluster
description: One of the largest and brightest globular clusters visible in the northern sky.

name: Double Cluster
description: Two dazzling open clusters close together, visible to the naked eye.

name: Praesepe Cluster
description: A large, nearby open cluster also known as the Beehive Cluster.

name: Wild Duck Cluster
description: One of the most massive and compact open clusters known, appearing like a flying flock of ducks.

name: Omega Centauri
description: The largest and brightest globular cluster in the Milky Way.

name: Jewel Box Cluster
description: A young open cluster with a colorful array of supergiant stars.

name: Globular Cluster M15
description: One of the densest globular clusters known in the Milky Way.

name: Open Cluster M35
description: A relatively large and bright open cluster easily visible in binoculars.
